minutes.headline: Cemetery Commission sought ARPA money for a North Cemetery stone wall; board took no vote and noted little ARPA remains.
minutes.summary: The board heard a joint presentation from the Cemetery Commission on replacing the failing North Cemetery hedge with a fieldstone wall funded from ARPA. Members praised it but said little ARPA remains and urged public outreach. The board also reviewed draft special town meeting articles, authorized town counsel to respond to a zoning appeal, approved an easement, and heard a town manager report on vacancies, flood response and health insurance projections.

what_happened.line: The Select Board heard a Cemetery Commission request for ARPA money to replace the failing North Cemetery hedge with a fieldstone wall, and took no vote.
A member said little ARPA money remains, and the board encouraged public outreach on the wall proposal.
The board authorized town counsel to respond to the 15 Cliff View Terrace appeal in Worcester Superior Court, and approved signing the 895 Flat Hill Road easement; both votes were not audible.
The board reviewed draft special town meeting articles, including a vehicle stabilization transfer, sewer stabilization transfers and a revised-scope transfer for primary school ductless systems.
The town manager was advised to budget an increase for active health insurance plans in FY25 and to expect similar increases for five years.

why_it_matters: Little ARPA money remains, so a request to fund the North Cemetery wall from it may not succeed, and a different funding source could mean a question at a town meeting.

The draft special town meeting articles on vehicle purchases, sewer transfers and school ductless systems are what residents may be asked to vote on, and they draw on stabilization and capital plan funds.
The health insurance advice points to rising premium costs across several years, which is a pressure on future town and school budgets.
watch_next: The Thursday Select Board meeting, where the Oktoberfest license date request was to be added to the agenda.
The next Select Board meeting, where members agreed to review a list and map of Select Board land after the site visits.

reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on both votes, the sewer transfers and most cemetery and storm figures, and the main differences are misheard names. The one to check is the $986,000 vehicle transfer, which only our minutes give, along with the dog bylaw next step (town counsel versus police chief feedback).
